blocks.value: Java is a high-level programming language developed by Sun Microsystems for general-purpose business applications and interactive, web-based Internet applications. Java programs can run on any operating system or device.
The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) is what makes this possible — it translates Java bytecode (the compiled form of a Java program) into machine language and executes it.

Here's how source code becomes a running program: you write source code in a text editor or development environment (like NetBeans), the Java compiler converts it into bytecode, and the Java interpreter — running inside the JVM — checks that bytecode and communicates with the operating system to execute it line by line.

There are two types of Java programs: an Application (a stand-alone program — either a console application that runs in a command-line window, or a windowed application with a GUI), and an Applet (a program embedded in a web page that runs inside a browser).
